data.narrative:
Lumaril is a Seed-stage robotics and manufacturing company founded by Mark Elliot and Ben Duffield that has raised $12M to date. The broader Robotics & Manufacturing sector comprises 10 private peers and 1 public comparable (277810.KQ), though the immediate peer set lacks sufficient depth for robust median-based valuation.

Stage-progression analysis, the primary applicable methodology, applies a 2.5x step-up multiplier to the $12M raised proxy, implying a $30M valuation at the next funding stage. This method reflects typical economics for Seed-stage advancement in the sector. Peer-median analysis was not executable due to insufficient same-stage and adjacent-stage comparables within the narrowly-filtered peer universe; relying on the full 10-company sector median would introduce unacceptable noise given valuation dispersion across robotics substrates and business models.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $26M to $34M, centered on $30M. This range reflects single-method triangulation, which constrains precision. Key uncertainties include the absence of tighter stage-cohort peers, limited public market reference points, and the heterogeneity of the Robotics & Manufacturing sector itself. Refinement would benefit from additional Seed-stage comparables or clearer subsector taxonomy within the peer set.
